title: OpenCRISPR-1 Becomes the First Fully AI-Designed Gene Editor Validated in Human Cells
aiSystem: Profluent Large-Scale CRISPR Protein Language Model
whyItMatters: Published in Nature, Profluent’s OpenCRISPR-1 is the first CRISPR-Cas genome editor generated entirely from scratch by AI—over 400 mutations from SpCas9—editing human DNA with lower off-target cuts.
summary: First open-sourced by Profluent in April 2024 and published in Nature in July 2025 (Ruffolo et al., Nature 645: 518–525), OpenCRISPR-1 demonstrated that protein language models trained on millions of natural CRISPR operons can design functional gene-editing enzymes entirely from scratch. Sitting >400 amino-acid mutations away from canonical SpCas9 (and ~200 mutations away from any known natural Cas protein), OpenCRISPR-1 matched SpCas9 editing efficiency in human cells while cutting off-target activity by up to 95%, and was released openly for broad research and therapeutic exploration.
technicalHighlights: Generated a complete, functional Cas9-like genome editor and guide RNA from scratch—more than 400 mutations away from SpCas9 and ~200 from any known natural protein.
Matched canonical SpCas9 on-target human-genome editing efficiency in wet-lab experiments while sharply reducing off-target cleavage.
Publicly released alongside the largest open CRISPR-Cas atlas to accelerate license-free AI-engineered gene and base editors.
caveats: Demonstrated in human cell lines (including base-editing fusions) rather than clinical human trials; long-term in vivo immunogenicity and delivery remain under study.

scoreRationale.foundational: Crossed a historic threshold in synthetic biology: moving gene editing from mining bacterial nature to generating wholly synthetic CRISPR enzymes with AI.
scoreRationale.ripple: Opens patent-unencumbered, customizable gene editors engineered for specificity and lower immunogenicity across therapeutics.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (645: 518–525) with extensive human-cell editing, off-target profiling, and open-source sequence release.
scoreRationale.velocity: Designed a highly divergent functional CRISPR nuclease in silico without decades of microbial bioprospecting or directed evolution.
